data.name: Manish
data.gender_notes: Manish is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manish comes from the Sanskrit word 'manas', which means 'mind'. The name is derived from the root 'manas' and is used to signify intellect or the power of thought. In Hindu mythology, Manish is also the name of a sage and a king. The name Manish carries the meaning “Mind, Intellect” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Manish usually hope their child will grow to embody mind, intellect and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of the mind and intellect.
data.etymology: Manish belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mind, Intellect.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manish total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Manish holds deep cultural significance in Hindu society as it is derived from the esteemed Sanskrit language. It is often given to children as a reminder of the importance of intellect and the power of thought. The name also has literary and mythological connections, emphasizing the heritage and richness of Hindu tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Manish signifies the connection between the individual soul and the Divine Consciousness. It highlights the importance of using one's intellect and mind to seek Enlightenment and ultimately merge with the Divine. In Hindu philosophy, the term Manas or the 'human mind', is often used to mention the incarnation of the Divine, emphasizing the ultimate Truth that the Divine is present within every being.

historical_references.reference: Manish was a popular Jain monk and scholar during the 12th to 13th centuries in India. He is best known for his work 'Sarva-dharma-sangraha', a comprehensive encyclopedia of Jain beliefs and practices.

Manish was a prominent Hindu king of the Satavahana dynasty, ruling from around 175 to 183 AD. He is known for his patronage of Buddhism and his role in the spreading of Buddhist art and culture in the region.
